narrative_summary: Global geopolitics and domestic governance are increasingly defined by transactional corruption, shifting alliances, and the erosion of traditional democratic norms. At an international summit in Shenzhen, President Trump met alongside Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, reinforcing concerns that U.S. foreign policy increasingly aligns with adversarial interests at the expense of Ukraine and Western security. Concurrently, the abrupt ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over national security breaches and ties to Chinese entities highlights the volatile intersection of corporate governance, personalist power, and advanced technology controls. Domestically, the Trump administration faces mounting investigations into widespread self-dealing, war profiteering, and the systematic dismantling of federal oversight structures. These compounding political strains coincide with economic anxieties, ranging from SNAP benefit theft and housing affordability crises to the staggering cultural and commercial footprint of Grand Theft Auto VI.

source_summaries.title: Anne Applebaum: All the Corruption, All the Time
bullets: Jared Kushner is accused of war profiteering by investing in defense contractors tied to conflicts he attempts to resolve.
The Trump administration faces allegations of receiving bribes from foreign regimes while holding inconsequential summits.
Democrats prepare to investigate extensive corruption linked to the White House over the next two years.

source_summaries.title: BREAKING: JD Vance Just Gave Trump the Answer He Didn’t Want to Hear on the Iran War
bullets: President Trump held a nearly two-hour marathon press conference following his summit with Putin and Xi.
During the event, JD Vance declined to state whether the Iran war was worth the cost of losing the Senate.
The press conference also featured praise for foreign dictators and what appeared to be a 2028 audition by Stephen Miller.

source_summaries.title: Trump Insider Jason Miller Is Making a Staggering Amount of Money
bullets: A child support lawsuit revealed that Trump insider Jason Miller secured a $15 million financial windfall.
Journalists Catherine Rampell and Sam Stein examined the expanding trend of individuals profiting from the Trump presidency.
The administration is actively working to dismantle government oversight structures.

source_summaries.title: America Is Part of the Axis of Evil
bullets: President Trump unexpectedly called into a meeting of European allies to criticize ongoing support for Ukraine and assert that Vladimir Putin is serious about negotiating peace.
U.S. officials at NATO talks told European nations they must defend themselves without relying on American forces while continuing to purchase U.S.-made weapons.
The article argues that current U.S. foreign policy effectively aligns with Russia against Ukraine and its Western allies.

source_summaries.title: Meet the Influencer Who Pissed Off Everyone in the Immigration Movement
bullets: Influencer Carlos Eduardo Espina sparked significant backlash within the immigration movement by floating a proposal to grant undocumented immigrants legal status while permanently barring them from voting.
Prominent Democratic organizers, activists, and the Congressional Black Caucus strongly condemned the idea, arguing it would create a vulnerable class of second-class citizens.
Espina defended his proposal, stating that many affected immigrants supported the idea and that professional activists are out of touch with the community.

source_summaries.title: The MAGA Crackup Around the Corner
bullets: Senate Republicans have increasingly blocked or stalled Trump nominees, such as T. Elliott Gaiser, Eric Ueland, and Heidi Overton, amid growing internal party friction.
Failed confirmations in the final weeks of the GOP trifecta risk handing future confirmation power over to incoming Senate Democrats.
Heidi Overton's withdrawn FDA nomination highlights deepening fractures between MAGA and MAHA factions, as well as impending party battles over abortion policy.

source_summaries.title: Why GTA VI Is the Biggest Cultural Event in a Decade
bullets: Grand Theft Auto VI generated more revenue in a single day than every movie ever released.
The game serves as a cultural touchstone that reflects the current state of America.
Video game criticism and the broader business of gaming present unique challenges for traditional critics.

source_summaries.title: The Dirty Bomb’s Real Power Is Fear
bullets: U.S. intelligence reports indicate that Iran is considering plans to use a dirty bomb targeting Washington, D.C., and senior Trump administration officials.
A dirty bomb combines conventional explosives with radioactive material, functioning primarily as a terror weapon rather than a nuclear-scale explosive.
While constructing and transporting a dirty bomb involves significant technical and logistical challenges, Iran and its proxies possess demonstrated capabilities to deploy advanced weaponry.

source_summaries.title: Live podcast — and a discount!
bullets: The hosts are hosting their first live podcast event on Wednesday, December 9, at the Miracle Theatre in Washington, D.C.
Paid subscribers to Slow Boring receive a discount code for approximately 40% off ticket prices.

source_summaries.title: The health insurance premium fix that everyone hates
bullets: Housing reform requires difficult coalition-building, careful attention to detail, and navigating politically powerful opposition with valid-sounding concerns like fire safety.
The Affordable Care Act prohibits insurers from denying coverage or charging exorbitant rates based on health risk to ensure sick people can get care.
Banning risk-based underwriting risks a death spiral where healthy people face sticker shock and drop out, though subsidies and preventive care coverage partially mitigate this issue.

source_summaries.title: REPLAY: Working with AI — with Billy Bennett
bullets: Billy Bennett demonstrates how the Prof G Media video team integrates artificial intelligence into their workflow.
The discussion covers AI applications ranging from thumbnail design and video clipping to unsuccessful experimental tools.
The full unedited replay of the session is available exclusively for Prof G+ subscribers.

source_summaries.title: There Is No (Business) God
bullets: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was forced out by his board following national security concerns regarding a customer suspected of spying for China and workplace policy violations.
Despite public petitions and defense from acolytes, Nvidia's board has refused to reinstate Huang, demonstrating that business leaders are mortal rather than divine.
Psychologically, humans transfer the childhood dependence on parents onto charismatic leaders and immortality projects to cope with the fear of mortality.

source_summaries.title: The Week: The Nvidia Cover-Up, Where Democrats Should Hit Hardest, and What an Expert on Power Says about Slowing Down
bullets: George Hahn discusses potential controversies involving the Commerce Department and Nvidia.
The publication outlines strategic priorities for the Democratic Congress.
The author of 'The 48 Laws of Power' advises against constant pursuit of success.

source_summaries.title: Why Aswath Damodaran Isn’t Buying Anthropic…Yet
bullets: Aswath Damodaran evaluates Nvidia's valuation, market position, and potential impacts of leadership changes.
He analyzes Anthropic's valuation while expressing specific concerns regarding its governance structure.
The discussion also covers notable stock market trends from the current year and forecasts the broader market outlook for 2027.

source_summaries.title: The Big Winner.
bullets: President Trump urged European leaders and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to make a peace deal with Russia so they could redirect funds to themselves.
Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected a return to ceasefire talks and vowed retaliation following recent Ukrainian missile strikes on a strategic bridge to Crimea.
President Putin emerged as a major diplomatic winner at a summit in Shenzhen, China, appearing alongside Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping without making compromises on the war.

source_summaries.title: A Texas Police Department Got $100K After a Single Immigration Arrest. It Stands to Earn Much More.
bullets: The police department in Pantego, Texas, received $100,000 from the federal government following a single immigration arrest under a 287(g) agreement with ICE.
Texas leads the nation with 429 law enforcement agencies participating in the program, which local officials frequently promote to city councils as a major source of funding.
Federal grants through the program reimburse everyday law enforcement operations, equipment, and payroll, raising concerns that small departments will become financially dependent on them.

source_summaries.title: Ohio Jobs Program Wants Its Money Back After Company’s Failure to Deliver GMO Salmon
bullets: JobsOhio is demanding the repayment of a $1 million grant after biotech company AquaBounty failed to complete a major GMO salmon production facility in Pioneer, Ohio.
The stalled project left AquaBounty with only three employees and $122,255 in cash by the end of September.
The venture faced regulatory hurdles, environmental pushback, and local scrutiny regarding land transactions involving the village mayor.

source_summaries.title: How SNAP Theft Happens — and What to Do if It Happens to You
bullets: SNAP recipients face widespread benefit theft through card skimming, phishing, and compromised state systems, with hundreds of millions of dollars stolen annually.
Criminals use skimming devices to capture magnetic strip data and PINs because EBT cards have been slow to adopt secure microchips and tap-to-pay technology.
Government inaction leaves individuals bearing the primary burden of protecting their benefits through monitoring apps and locking cards when not in use.

source_summaries.title: The next round of Supreme Court forecasts
bullets: The Supreme Court's third session of oral arguments for the 2026-27 term begins on November 30, featuring major cases such as Viramontes v. Cook County and Department of Homeland Security v. D.V.D.
SCOTUSblog is partnering with Good Judgment Inc. to host a forecasting challenge allowing the public and AI models to predict outcomes for key cases.
Participants can sign up online to forecast the outcomes of featured cases from both the October session and upcoming arguments.

source_summaries.title: Criminal law is constitutional law
bullets: A fundamental premise of criminal law, such as the requirement for proof beyond a reasonable doubt established in In re Winship, is rooted in constitutional law.
The standard of proof beyond a reasonable doubt is constitutionally required by the Due Process Clause despite not being mentioned textually in the Constitution or Bill of Rights.
The Constitution does not contain a comprehensive criminal code and defines only a single federal crime, treason, leaving criminal law primarily to the states.

source_summaries.title: Even justices have regrets
bullets: Chief Justice Roberts and Justice Kavanaugh cited Sandra Day O'Connor's 2003 prediction that racial preferences would be unnecessary within 25 years when ruling against race-conscious admissions in 2023.
O'Connor later told her biographer that her 25-year timeline may have been a misjudgment and stated there is actually no timetable for when such measures will become unnecessary.

source_summaries.title: Trump administration brings climate grant dispute to SCOTUS
bullets: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to allow the EPA to cancel $16 billion in Biden-era climate grants.
The disputed funds were awarded under a 2022 law for clean energy projects before the Trump administration rescinded them.
A divided federal appeals court previously ruled in August that the administration improperly terminated the grants.

source_summaries.source: Heather Cox Richardson from Letters from an American
source_summaries.title: Preparing for Investigations
bullets: The provided article text consists entirely of promotional metadata, subscription links, and podcast access details without substantive content.
No factual arguments or policy points were present in the source material to summarize.

source_summaries.title: GTA VI Shouldn’t Spark a Moral Panic. It Should Spark New Rules.
bullets: The massive launch of Grand Theft Auto VI raises valid concerns for parents and policymakers regarding video game safety for minors.
Addressing risks to young people requires focusing on problematic design elements such as predatory spending, addictive mechanics, and stranger interactions rather than just content ratings.
Policymakers and industry observers argue that making games safer necessitates regulating harmful structural design features rather than yielding to recurring moral panics over violence.

source_summaries.title: For the Renewal of Conservatism
bullets: The author argues that the Republican midterm election losses present an opportunity for a necessary renewal of conservatism and a return to fundamental political principles.
A renewed conservatism must prioritize personal character in leadership, respect for the rule of law, and adherence to constitutional processes and democratic norms.
The article asserts that the conservative movement must reject election denialism and uncritical loyalty to Donald Trump in favor of truth-telling and genuine patriotism.

source_summaries.title: Is the Electoral College About to End?
bullets: Some Democrats are exploring a workaround to effectively bypass the Electoral College without a constitutional amendment.
The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact aims to have states award their electoral votes to the winner of the national popular vote once participating states total at least 270 electoral votes.
Eighteen states and the District of Columbia have joined the compact, bringing the total to 222 electoral votes as organizers target remaining states to reach the threshold.

source_summaries.title: What powered Democratic gains with Latinos in 2026?
bullets: Latino voters swung significantly toward Democrats in the 2026 midterms, erasing the gains Donald Trump made with this demographic in 2024.
In heavily Hispanic House districts, the Democratic margin jumped by approximately 22 points compared to the 2024 presidential results.
The substantial shift back to the Democratic party challenges previous theories that the 2024 election represented a permanent racial realignment in American politics.

source_summaries.title: Three’s a Crowd (November 20, 2026)
bullets: Xi Jinping hosted a notable three-way meeting in Shenzhen with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin during the APEC forum.
The leaders issued a Declaration of Peace calling for UN reform and nuclear opposition, though the gathering yielded no substantive progress on ongoing conflicts or arms control.
The actions of China, Russia, and the United States continue to undermine nuclear nonproliferation prospects despite their rhetorical opposition to it.

source_summaries.title: Embarassing and Inconsequential
bullets: President Trump participated in a summit in Shenzhen alongside Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping that produced no serious agreements or relief for Ukraine.
The meeting functioned primarily as a Chinese propaganda event designed to generate flattering photographs and video clips.
Trump praised the pageantry of his airport greeting by Xi Jinping as a major diplomatic win despite the lack of substantive outcomes.

source_summaries.title: Grand Expectations
bullets: Grand Theft Auto VI has officially launched to overwhelmingly positive reviews, debuting with a score of 99 on Metacritic.
Development costs for the highly anticipated game are estimated to exceed $1 billion, with total investments potentially reaching up to $2 billion.
Despite the critical and commercial success of GTA VI, the article questions whether parent company Take-Two will necessarily remain a strong investment.

source_summaries.title: Why Are Tech Lords Rallying Around a Man Who Sold Out America?
bullets: Prominent tech leaders are vociferously supporting disgraced former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and demanding his reinstatement.
Jensen Huang had an extended affair with Alice Huang, a likely Chinese asset and controlling shareholder of a data center company providing compute to Chinese entities.
Nvidia systematically undermined U.S. security by lobbying to relax export restrictions and selling advanced chips to Chinese companies, including those with military ties.

source_summaries.title: Sex, lies, and export controls
bullets: The abrupt downfall of Nvidia's Jensen Huang highlights the chaotic intersection of export controls, corporate greed, and personalist governance.
Export controls function through a complex regulatory scheme involving multiple federal agencies to restrict the sale of sensitive technology to foreign adversaries.
While Donald Trump campaigned on a tough stance against China, his administration's shift toward unilateral decision-making enabled corruption and policy inconsistencies regarding chip exports.

source_summaries.title: Man vs. Machine
bullets: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar discusses topics ranging from sports and media to political developments involving Donald Trump and international leaders.
The publication previews a documentary by Alex Gibney examining Elon Musk using his own words and an AI avatar.
The text profiles early 20th-century writer and publisher Elbert Hubbard, tracing his journey from a successful salesman to the founder of the Roycroft artisan community.

source_summaries.title: Anthropic’s IPO in Pictures
bullets: Anthropic completed the largest IPO in history, debuting with a market capitalization of $1.8 trillion and closing its first day of trading at $97.17 per share.
The five-year-old AI startup sold 980 million shares at $83 each, achieving a brief valuation of over $2 trillion during its market entry.
The IPO occurred amid an AI bear market and high financial debt-to-equity ratios, drawing attention to the stark contrast between rapid commercial expansion and existential safety warnings.

source_summaries.title: Democrats: Drain Trump’s Swamp!
bullets: Robert Reich argues that incoming congressional Democrats must conduct oversight hearings to expose and reverse the corruption and moral rot of the Trump administration.
The article highlights various conflicts of interest and self-dealing by Donald Trump, including hosting a G20 summit at his private golf club and monetizing market-altering announcements.
Reich criticizes Trump for praising authoritarian leaders like Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping while seeking to undermine international accountability for human rights violations.
